Plasmodiumfalciparum mature male and female gametocytes can circulate in vitro for up to at least 14 and 16–32 days, respectively, and the average 50% gametocyte survival time is 6.5–2.6 and at least 3.5 days, respectively.

Plasmodiumfalciparum gameteocytes survive up to two months (16-32 days) in vitro, in absence of the host influence, which is in agreement with the previous mathematical model that was based on molecular tools for the detection of gametocytes in treated patients.
P. falciparium gametocytes can live up to 2 months in vitro and this is the first study that experimentally confirmed the longevity of gametocyte in vitro.
